script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination 2027. English Language Paper 3. Listening and Integrated Skills. The Staycation Revolution.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Part A. Task 1. You are at the check-in counter for the 'Future Tourism Expo'. You will hear a conversation between a registration clerk and an exhibitor. Complete the form. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Good morning, sir. Welcome to the Expo. We're expecting a massive turnout for the Eco-Tourism track this year. Can I have your company details for the badge?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Morning. I'm Marcus Thorpe, T-H-O-R-P-E. I'm representing Wilderness Retreats Ltd. We're the ones setting up the glamping pods in the courtyard.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Wilderness Retreats... right. And for our records, your direct contact email? Is it still the info address?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: No, please use my personal work one. It's m.thorpe@wilderness.com.hk. That's M-dot-T-H-O-R-P-E at wilderness dot com dot hk.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Got it. Now, you're registered under the Eco-Glamping Pavilion, correct? I have you assigned to Hall 3C. That's on the third floor, just next to the escalators.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Perfect. Hall 3C. And about the display... we originally planned for five tents, but because of the space constraints in that hall, we've scaled it back to 3 display tents. One dome tent, one safari style, and a bell tent.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Noted. Three tents. Now, for the equipment rental, you requested some laptops for the interactive booking demo. Do you still need six?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Actually, our tech team brought their own tablets, so we only need four laptops from you now. However, we do need a specific power supply. The standard 110V won't run our climate control demo. We need 220V High Voltage.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: I'll make a note for the technicians. 220V. Also, you have a media interview slot booked for the weekend... Oh wait, it's been moved. It's now scheduled for Friday at 2:00 PM with the 'Urban Traveler' magazine.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Friday at 2:00. I'll be there. One more thing, here is my insurance policy number for the setup. It's WR-9988-X.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: WR-9988-X. Perfect. I see you've already received the 15% Early Bird discount on your booth fee. However, the final payment status shows as 'Bank Transfer Pending'. You might want to check with your accounts department.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: I'll do that right away. Thanks for the heads up.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 2. Listen to a podcast episode regarding 'The Glamping Boom in the New Territories'. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Welcome to 'Nature HK'. Today we're talking about staycations. Forget five-star hotels; it's all about glamping now. We currently have 42 registered sites across the New Territories. While Sai Kung was the pioneer, Yuen Long has overtaken it as the most popular district due to the availability of flat farmland. At an average nightly rate of $1800, it's not cheap, but young families are flocking there to give their kids a taste of the outdoors without the mud.

script.speaker: Expert
script.text: That's right. But it's not all easy money. Operators tell me waste management is their biggest headache—getting garbage trucks into remote sites is tough. While bookings are steady, Autumn is definitely the peak season; the weather is just perfect for sitting outside. Legally, you can't just pitch a tent; you need a Short Term Tenancy permit from the Lands Department and a Fire Safety Type B certificate. People come for the star-gazing experience, which is why we are seeing a 22% annual growth. Next on the map? A huge new project in Lantau South in collaboration with the Eco-Travel Association.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 3. Three experts are debating 'Traditional Hotels vs. Glamping'. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Prof Ng
script.text: I still maintain that for a city like Hong Kong, our heritage hotels are indispensable. You can't replace the Peninsula's history with a plastic dome. Look at the data: traditional hotel occupancy is still respectable at 68%.

script.speaker: Mr Lau
script.text: But Professor, people are tired of concrete boxes. The main concern with hotels is the total lack of nature. Glamping occupancy is at 85%! People want to breathe. That's why I'm pushing for the $500 million subsidy for eco-tourism development.

script.speaker: Ms Cheung
script.text: Why not a compromise? A hybrid model. Hotels could install tented villas on their balconies or grounds. We should have a minimum guest age of 6 years old for these to ensure safety, and a strict noise limit of 55 decibels. We should also encourage hotels to get the EarthCheck Gold certification to stay competitive. Our main revenue for hotels used to be business travelers, but the future is leisure weekends.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 4. Stakeholders discussing wild camping. (240-second pause)

script.speaker: Environmentalist
script.text: We are seeing severe soil erosion in protected zones. We need drones for patrols. The 2025 Biodiversity Audit proved the damage is real.

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: And the trash! I'm tired of cleaning up after tourists. We want a $3,000 fine for littering and permit-only parking for us villagers. 1823-CAMP should be the line for complaints.

script.speaker: Operator
script.text: I suggest a digital permit system to limit group sizes to 8 people. We're happy to carry third-party indemnity insurance if it means we can keep operating. We expect the full regulations by January 2027 after the public consultation.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Part B. Integrated Skills Recording. Listen to the briefing from the Director of the Staycation Bureau to the Senior Project Manager.

script.speaker: Director
script.text: Alright, let's get moving on these tasks. We have some delicate issues to handle. First, Task 8—when you write to the 'Save Our Greenery' group, don't just talk about the economy. They are worried about the local fauna. Make sure you mention that our new glamping guidelines require the use of 'Invisible Fencing'. This is a special technology that keeps the site boundaries secure without blocking the natural migration of small animals. It's a huge environmental plus that isn't in the brochures yet.

script.speaker: Director
script.text: For the internal memo in Task 9, we need to address the low uptake of the staycation vouchers in rural areas. I want you to propose a 'Midnight Discount Scheme'. If guests book between midnight and 6:00 AM for last-minute slots, they get an extra 20% off. It helps fill the tents during the week. Also, mention we are implementing a 'Quiet Hours' policy starting strictly at 10:00 PM across all sites to appease the villagers. This is vital for the memo.

script.speaker: Director
script.text: Finally, for Task 10, the social media post needs to be punchy. I've come up with a slogan I want you to use: 'Wild Luxury, Local Heart'. It sums up the balance we're aiming for. Oh, and mention our new partnership with the 'Star-Seeker App'. It's an app that helps guests identify constellations from their tents. It adds value to the experience. Get those drafts to me by five. Thanks.

data_file.title: Minutes: Rural Tourism Development Meeting
data_file.content: Date: May 12, 2027. Points: 1. Residents in Yuen Long complained about light pollution from glamping sites. 2. Need for 'Dark Sky' compliant lighting. 3. Promotion of Green Staycation Vouchers ($1000 subsidy).

data_file.title: Starry Nights Glamping: Guest Guide
data_file.content: Experience the NT like never before. 100% solar powered. Nightly stargazing tours. Please note: No loud music after 9 PM. All trash must be carried out. Nightly rate: $1950 (weekend).

data_file.title: Email from Ms. Gladys Ho (Resident)
data_file.content: To: Staycation Bureau. Subject: Light Pollution. The new glamping site near Kam Tin is like a football stadium at night. My children can't sleep. The floodlights are pointed right at the village. Do something!

data_file.title: The Daily Post: Hotels vs. Tents
data_file.content: Traditional hotels in Tsim Sha Tsui are struggling with 60% occupancy, while New Territories glamping sites are fully booked months in advance. Experts suggest hotels must 'go green' or go bust.

data_file.title: Note from Director
data_file.content: PM: Re: Gladys Ho's email. Tell her we're mandating 'Down-Shield' lights by next month. Also, mention the 10 PM quiet rule from the briefing. We must keep the villagers happy.

data_file.title: Internal Memo: Licensing Update
data_file.content: New regulation: All sites must have a 1:10 staff-to-guest ratio. Must provide eco-friendly toiletries. Waste must be sorted into four categories.

data_file.title: The Heritage Inn: Traditional Charm
data_file.content: Stay in a converted 1920s mansion. Full AC. Fine dining. No tents here! Discount for seniors available.

data_file.title: Draft: Green Staycation Vouchers
data_file.content: Subsidy can only be used at certified 'Eco-Sites'. Sites must prove 20% reduction in plastic use within 6 months of joining the scheme.
